title: Should the Fouled Player Take the Penalty Himself?
excerpt: A player gets fouled by the GK and walks straight to the spot. Should he? Theory says no — jarred, agitated, while the keeper is locked in. A one-tailed z-test on 79 treatment penalties vs 3,456 controls in the top 5 European leagues.
finding: When the fouled player takes the penalty himself, conversion drops 3.0 pp (75.95% vs 78.96%) — but with only 79 such cases the data can't yet say 'hand it to someone else' (p = 0.26, one-tailed).

title: Not All Goals Are Equal: A Time-Aware Expected-Points Model
excerpt: A goal from 0–0 to 1–0 in the fifth minute and the same goal in the eighty-fifth are not the same thing. Expected points (EP) prices every goal by the goal-difference transition it produced and the minute it landed — across 39,381 goals in six top-flight leagues and seven seasons.
finding: A goal's value depends on the minute as well as the scoreline: a late go-ahead goal from level is worth far more than an early opener.

title: The True Contributors: Who Actually Moves the Table?
excerpt: Applies the expected-points value model from project 02 to rank players whose true contribution diverges from their box-score reputation. Scorer, assist-creator and pre-assist-creator all credited.
finding: Julian Brandt creates more pre-assist value than any player in Europe except Lionel Messi — 40.93 EP from SCA2 alone, 39% of his total contribution.
